Tech Stocks Fall as Next Week Brings Big Tests for the AI Trade
 
Plus, Nvidia declines and Anthropic CEO hopes IPO will “overdeliver”
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
CHUNG SUNG-JUN/GETTY IMAGES
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Tech stocks slumped and Nvidia shares gave up early gains to turn red again as investors brace for further fallout from the crisis. Chip and data-center stocks sold off. Nvidia closed down 2%. Nvidia is due to report earnings on Tuesday and interim CEO Colette Kress will face questions about the web of financing deals that Huang struck.

The Nasdaq closed 0.9% lower. Shares in Microsoft recovered to be little changed after dropping earlier as it works to resolve a widespread outage that is affecting its Teams and Outlook services. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Dow gained 0.1%.

 

Oil prices ticked higher as traders keep a close eye on the Mideast conflict. A selloff in bond markets abated Friday after Treasury yields rose sharply yesterday on solidifying expectations of further interest-rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. Longer-dated yields are still ticking up. The Labor Department said Friday that wholesale prices rose by 0.3% in October, cooling sharply from their 1.4% increase in September. Even so, the increase raised the 12-month wholesale inflation rate to a blistering 6.5%, from 6.3% in September.

 

Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei said he hopes the company will “underpromise and overdeliver” in its initial public offering. Amodei made the comments while speaking Friday in a livestreamed fireside chat with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon. The maker of the popular Claude chatbot, Anthropic is targeting a valuation of roughly $1.33 trillion or more, and its shares are expected to begin trading Thursday.

One Big Story

 
 
DAVID PAUL MORRIS
 

Nvidia is the most valuable company to abruptly lose a leader so instrumental to its fortunes—but it is hardly the first.

 

Apple lost founder-and-rescuer Steve Jobs to cancer. McDonald’s abruptly fired Steve Easterbrook, alleging an improper relationship with a subordinate. Nissan dropped Carlos Ghosn as chairman in 2018, just after police arrested him in Tokyo on allegations of financial misconduct and underreporting his income.

 

The danger of losing a seemingly indispensable leader is known as key-person risk in investor parlance, and some companies have lost hundreds of millions in market value after losing their key men.

Anthropic makes it stock market debut next week and what could be one of the biggest IPOs of all time. WSJ’s David Wainer explains how the public offering could affect the entire U.S. economy.

 
 
 

What’s Coming Up

 

• Nvidia is due to report earnings on Tuesday, when finance chief and interim CEO Colette Kress will face questions about the web of financing deals that Huang struck.

 

• Anthropic, one of the biggest users of Nvidia’s chips, is expected to start trading on Thursday.

 

• Fed meeting minutes will be released on Wednesday. Traders will dissect this for cues on upcoming rate decisions.
